entries.summary: Adds/updates section(s): August 2026; 1.5.3; July 2026

Adds/updates section(s): Prerequisites; Step 1: Enable GPU profiling via the Inspektor Gadget extension; Step 2: Enable profile visualization with Pyroscope Changes CLI flags: ---, --version, --name, --configuration-settings Adds runnable examples (e.g., az grafana data-source create \). Includes security/operational guidance (Key Vault/managed identity/NSG).
Changes CLI flags: --version
Changes CLI flags: ----------------------, -------------------, ------------------, ------------- Includes security/operational guidance (Key Vault/managed identity/NSG).
Adds/updates section(s): Verify the ALB Controller installation; Verify ALB Controller Pods; Verify GatewayClass Includes security/operational guidance (Key Vault/managed identity/NSG).
Changes CLI flags: --version
Learn how to analyze GPU profiling flame graphs to identify functions that consume the most GPU memory in workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service.
The Get-AksEdgeDeploymentInfo PowerShell command retrieves information about AKS Edge deployments, providing users with essential details for managing their deployments.

The Update-AksHci PowerShell command documentation has been removed, which may affect users who need to update their AKS hybrid environments. This change suggests a shift in how updates are managed within AKS.

The documentation now includes a section on restoring Helm v3 default behavior when using the `helm-controller` with `microsoft.flux` v1.25.0, which defaults to Helm v4. Users can enable the `useHelm3Defaults` setting via the `az k8s-extension update` command to revert to Helm v3 defaults if their releases are incompatible with Helm v4 changes. This provides a temporary solution while users validate their Helm releases against the new defaults.

Corrected the link for the kata technical documentation from an outdated URL to the current one, ensuring users have access to the latest resources. This change improves the accuracy of the documentation.

The 'Install-AksHciMonitoring' command is introduced, which deploys a Prometheus-based monitoring solution for AKS hybrid. This command is essential for users looking to implement monitoring in their deployments, providing necessary parameters and examples.

The Start-AksEdgeUpdate PowerShell command initiates the update process for AKS Edge Essentials nodes. It includes syntax, parameters, and examples for updating nodes, emphasizing the need for user confirmation unless the Force parameter is specified.

A new document has been added that provides guidance on how to list pods in an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster using kubectl. It covers listing pods in various namespaces, filtering by label, and includes examples for better understanding.
The Get-AksEdgeUpgrade PowerShell command checks if AKS Edge Essentials is allowed to upgrade the Kubernetes version on update. It includes syntax and examples for usage.

The Remove-AksHciGmsaCredentialSpec PowerShell command documentation has been revised to provide clearer instructions on deleting credentials specs for gMSA deployments, including syntax and examples.
This document has been updated to restructure the troubleshooting guidance for AKS API server connection issues, enhancing clarity and usability for users facing connectivity problems.

The Repair-AksHciClusterCerts PowerShell command is designed to troubleshoot and fix errors related to expired certificates for Kubernetes built-in components. This update emphasizes the deprecation of this cmdlet and suggests using Update-AksHciClusterCertificates instead, providing important guidance for users managing certificate issues.
Removed the entire document related to the Copy-AksEdgeNodeFile PowerShell command, which included details on copying files to or from a node.

The Disable-AksHciArcConnection command documentation has been removed, which may impact users managing Arc connections in their AKS hybrid clusters. This change suggests a reevaluation of how connections are handled.
The Connect-AksEdgeArc PowerShell command adds the cluster to Azure Arc, enabling centralized management and monitoring of AKS Edge clusters.

This document describes the Enable-AksHciOfflineDownload command, which enables offline downloading of AKS hybrid images. This is beneficial for deployments in environments with limited internet access.

The documentation for the Container Registry RBAC built-in roles has been updated to clarify the permissions associated with managing and viewing repository-level policies for images and artifact streaming configurations. Users can now see that specific roles grant permissions to manage and view these policies, enhancing their understanding of role capabilities within the registry. This change improves clarity on how users can interact with repository-level policies and artifact streaming settings.

The Set-AksEdgeUpgrade PowerShell command sets whether AKS Edge Essentials is allowed to upgrade the Kubernetes version on update. It includes syntax, parameters, and examples for configuring the upgrade acceptance.
The New-AksEdgeDeployment PowerShell command creates a new deployment in an existing AKS Edge cluster. It includes syntax and examples for usage.

The Install-AksHciCsiNfs PowerShell command installs the CSI NFS Plugin to a cluster, with detailed syntax and examples provided. This command is essential for users looking to enhance their AKS hybrid deployments with NFS capabilities.
Removed the entire document related to the Add-AksEdgeNode PowerShell command, which included details on adding a new AksEdge node to the cluster.
Removed the entire document related to the Invoke-AksEdgeNodeCommand PowerShell command, which included details on executing an SSH command on the VM.
The document has been archived, indicating that the Disable-AksHciOfflinedownload PowerShell command is no longer available for use.

The Get-AksHciProxySetting PowerShell command retrieves a proxy configuration for AKS hybrid. It provides examples and notes on the limitations of proxy settings, emphasizing that only one settings object can be active at a time.

The Update-AksHciCluster PowerShell command documentation has been revised to clarify the process of updating a managed Kubernetes cluster to a newer Kubernetes or OS version. This includes syntax and examples for better user guidance.
The Remove-AksHciClusterNetwork PowerShell command removes a virtual network from the system, which is critical for managing network resources in AKS hybrid environments.
The document has been archived, indicating that the Remove-AksEdgeNode PowerShell command is no longer available for use.
The release notes for Flux GitOps have been updated to include the latest version details, changes related to Helm v4, and security updates across various controllers.

The documentation for configuring a custom private DNS zone in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) has been updated to clarify that AKS will create a virtual network link for the spoke VNet hosting the cluster, even if the DNS zone is already linked to a hub VNet. Users must ensure that the cluster's managed identity has **Network Contributor** permissions on the spoke VNet before setting `publicDNS` to `false` or using `--disable-public-fqdn`.

Added a note regarding the NSG enforcement model when an association is deleted and recreated, emphasizing the importance of configuring NSG allow rules to avoid connectivity issues. This update enhances the clarity and usability of the documentation.

This document outlines the Test-AksEdgeNetworkParameters PowerShell command, which validates AKS Edge network parameters as a pre-deployment step, ensuring that configurations are correct before scaling clusters.
The Remove-AksHciCluster command deletes a managed Kubernetes cluster, providing users with the ability to cleanly remove clusters that are no longer needed.

This document describes the New-AksHciNodePool PowerShell command, which allows users to create a new node pool in an existing AKS cluster. This is essential for scaling and managing resources effectively in AKS.

A new article has been added that lists supported kubelet and OS configuration parameters for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) node pools using Custom Node Configuration. It provides detailed descriptions of parameters and their implications for cluster management.

Merged changes from the main branch, which likely included updates to the PowerShell command documentation for retrieving AKS hybrid logs, enhancing the usability and accuracy of the command reference.

The Update-AksHciCertificates PowerShell command rotates tokens and certificates of all clients in the AKS hybrid host. This command is crucial for maintaining security and compliance within AKS environments.
The Get-AksHciRegistration PowerShell command is explained in this document, which retrieves registration information for AKS hybrid deployments, essential for managing hybrid environments.

The Start-AksEdgeControlPlaneUpdate PowerShell command updates control plane nodes as part of the upgrade process, ensuring that the cluster remains up-to-date with the latest features and security patches.

The documentation for customizing node configurations in AKS has been updated to clarify the prerequisites for using preview kubelet settings, specifically `kubeReserved` and `hardEvictionThreshold`. Users are now informed that these settings require the `CustomNodeConfigPreview` feature flag and must register it using the Azure CLI. Additionally, the sections on creating clusters and adding node pools have been refined to emphasize the need for specifying configuration files for both Linux and Windows node pools, ensuring users understand how to apply custom configurations effectively.
The Test-AksEdgeArcConnection PowerShell command checks whether the cluster is Azure Arc-connected, which is vital for ensuring proper integration with Azure services.
The Get-AksHciVmSize PowerShell command retrieves available VM sizes for AKS hybrid. It includes syntax, parameters, and examples for selecting appropriate VM sizes for deployments.
This document details the Disconnect-AksEdgeArc PowerShell command, which removes an AKS Edge Essentials cluster from Azure Arc, providing necessary steps and parameters for proper execution.

The known issues documentation for AKS has been updated to reflect changes in the status of various issues, including fixes in specific releases. The document now includes updated references to issues related to the AKS telemetry pod and cluster creation problems.
The Remove-AksEdgeDeployment PowerShell command removes the deployment from an existing cluster. It includes syntax and parameters for usage.
Removed the entire document related to the New-AksHciClusterNetwork PowerShell command, which included details on creating a virtual network for workload clusters.

Updates include changes to the scaling sizes for AKS clusters, with new details on the performance metrics for H2, H4, and H8 scaling sizes. The documentation now specifies the memory allocation in GiB instead of GB, and includes updated commands for installing and updating the 'aks-preview' extension.
The Uninstall-AksHciGmsaWebhook PowerShell command uninstalls the gMSA webhook add-on from the cluster. It provides a synopsis and usage details.
This document outlines known issues in AKS Hybrid and Edge on VMware, including workarounds and root cause descriptions, which are crucial for troubleshooting and ensuring smooth operations.
Merged changes from the main branch, ensuring the documentation is up-to-date with the latest information and best practices for configuring container network logs in AKS.
The Remove-AksHciNodePool PowerShell command deletes a node pool from a cluster. It includes syntax, parameters, and examples for usage, detailing how to specify the cluster name and node pool name.

The document provides a PowerShell command to retrieve the current version of AKS Hybrid. This is useful for users to ensure they are using the latest features and fixes available in their AKS deployments.

This document describes the Enable-AksHciPreview PowerShell command, which updates AKS hybrid to a preview channel. It includes usage examples and a note on the intended use of the preview channel for development and testing.
The Get-AksHciEventLog PowerShell command retrieves all event logs from the AKS hybrid PowerShell module, which is essential for monitoring and troubleshooting AKS environments.

The documentation now clarifies that for multi-rack deployments, users can utilize the `az aksarc get-credentials` command to retrieve a `kubeconfig` file, enhancing their ability to access AKS clusters. Additionally, it introduces Microsoft Entra integration, allowing users to manage access to Kubernetes resources using their Microsoft Entra credentials, thereby streamlining user account management and security within AKS clusters.

Users can now connect to an Azure RBAC-enabled AKS Arc cluster using either `az aksarc get-credentials` in direct mode or `az connectedk8s proxy` in proxy mode, with specific instructions provided for each method. The documentation clarifies that the first time a `kubectl` command is executed, users will be prompted to sign in with Microsoft Entra ID, and their requests will be authorized based on Azure role assignments. Additionally, it highlights that using the `--admin` flag with `az aksarc get-credentials` bypasses Azure RBAC, allowing access to a certificate-based admin kubeconfig.

The documentation has been updated to reflect the latest supported Kubernetes versions and component updates for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). Users can now utilize updated versions of critical components such as cilium-agent (v1.19.6), coredns (v1.14.3-3), and keda (v2.19.0-6), enhancing performance and security. Additionally, the cloud-provider-node-manager components have been upgraded to versions v1.36.1 for both Linux and Windows, providing improved resource management capabilities.
This article now includes a new section on Artifact Streaming, detailing how to stream container images from Azure Container Registry to AKS, along with prerequisites and configuration steps.

This document has been revised to improve troubleshooting guidance for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster upgrade and scaling errors. It now includes prerequisites and detailed descriptions of common causes of failure, enhancing the clarity and usability of the troubleshooting process.

The documentation now clarifies that users can request increases for specific limits related to Azure Container Registry, including registry storage limits, maximum private endpoints, and image push and pull performance limits. Additionally, it specifies which limits are fixed and cannot be increased through support requests, such as maximum public IP network rules and maximum non-Microsoft Entra token scope maps. This provides users with a clearer understanding of their options for scaling and performance enhancements.

The Set-AksHciAutoScalerProfile PowerShell command allows reconfiguration of an autoscaler configuration profile. This update includes detailed descriptions of parameters and examples for changing settings like min and max node counts, scan intervals, and more, which are crucial for managing autoscaling effectively.

The documentation now includes a comprehensive "Quick Reference Checklist" for enhancing AKS cluster reliability, which outlines critical best practices such as configuring Pod Disruption Budgets (PDBs), setting CPU and memory limits, deploying multiple replicas for zone-resilient workloads, and enabling Container Insights for monitoring. Additionally, it emphasizes the importance of enabling availability zones during cluster creation and using a Standard Load Balancer for production workloads, providing users with actionable steps to improve their cluster's availability and resilience.

The document details the 'New-AksHciSSHConfiguration' command, which creates an SSH configuration object for AKS-HCI virtual machines. This is crucial for defining SSH access, with examples provided for user guidance.

The documentation was updated to clarify the command for managing minor version updates of extensions. The previous command `--auto-upgrade-minor-version false` has been replaced with `--auto-upgrade-mode none`, which enhances clarity on how to control automatic upgrades.
The artifact streaming section has been enhanced to include details on enabling artifact streaming for Node Auto Provisioning (NAP) clusters, along with prerequisites and configuration instructions.

The Initialize-AksHciNode PowerShell command runs checks on every physical node to ensure all requirements are satisfied for installing AKS hybrid. This command is vital for preparing nodes for deployment.

The document describes the 'Get-AksEdgeLogs' PowerShell command, which collects logs from the AKS Edge deployment. This command is important for monitoring and troubleshooting, ensuring users can effectively manage their AKS Edge environments.

The Install-AksHci PowerShell command documentation has been removed, indicating a change in the installation process for AKS hybrid environments. Users may need to refer to alternative methods for installation.

The New-AksHciCluster PowerShell command creates a new managed Kubernetes cluster with various parameters including node pool name, node count, and Kubernetes version. It includes examples for creating clusters with different configurations, such as enabling monitoring and AD authentication.

The Set-AksHciOffsiteConfig command is detailed, which sets the offsite configuration for offline downloading of AKS hybrid images. This command is crucial for environments that require offline capabilities.

The document has been updated to clarify the scope of Fleet auto-upgrade profiles and improve the instructions for listing and managing these profiles. It now emphasizes that auto-upgrade profiles are Fleet-level resources, enhancing the understanding of their management.
The Sync-AksHciBilling command manually triggers a billing records sync, ensuring that billing information is up to date and accurate for AKS hybrid deployments.

This article provides guidance on monitoring and logging object events in AKS Hybrid and Edge on VMware. It emphasizes the importance of monitoring for operational efficiency and includes links to relevant documentation for further reading.

The Uninstall-AksHciAdAuth PowerShell command uninstalls Active Directory authentication from an AKS hybrid cluster. This command is important for users needing to manage authentication methods in their deployments.
The Restart-AksHci PowerShell command restarts AKS hybrid and removes all deployed Kubernetes clusters. It includes syntax and a description of the command's impact on existing clusters.

The Install-AksHciAdAuth PowerShell command documentation has been revised to provide clearer syntax and examples for installing Active Directory authentication in AKS hybrid environments. This includes detailed parameter descriptions.

The document outlines the 'Disable-AksHciPreview' command, which allows users to revert from a preview channel back to the stable channel. This includes important notes and examples, aiding users in managing their AKS hybrid deployments effectively.

The documentation for the "Zero-Downtime AKS Migration" runbook has been updated to improve accuracy and clarity. Users can now shift traffic progressively using relative DNS weights with Traffic Manager or precise request percentages with ingress or service mesh routing, and they are advised to hold each stage for a sufficient time to measure application traffic. Additionally, the instructions emphasize that clients may continue to use cached DNS responses until their TTL expires when routing back to the old endpoint.

The article has been updated to clarify network security best practices for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). It now includes detailed guidance on planning network policies, service exposure, ingress security, and API server access for production AKS clusters. The changes enhance the understanding of how to minimize unauthorized access and protect workloads.

The documentation has been updated to reflect the latest Cilium versions compatible with Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). Users can now see that Cilium versions 1.16.19, 1.17.18, 1.18.12, and 1.19.6 are available for LTS releases 1.31, 1.32, 1.34, 1.35, and 1.36, respectively, providing access to improved features and security updates.
The Get-AksEdgeNodeAddr command retrieves the IP and MAC addresses of the AKS Edge nodes, which is essential for network management and troubleshooting.

The Start-AksEdgeNode PowerShell command starts the node VM if it's currently stopped. This cmdlet is asynchronous and does not wait for the Kubernetes endpoint to be available, requiring users to wait before the endpoint is accessible.

The Get-AksEdgeNodeName PowerShell command retrieves the hostname of the VM based on the specified node type. It provides syntax and examples for usage, including parameters for specifying the node type.
The Get-AksHciBillingStatus PowerShell command retrieves the billing status for the AKS hybrid deployment. It includes syntax and examples for usage.

The documentation now includes a new section on dedicating node pools to multiple applications, providing detailed guidance on creating separate node pools with unique taints and labels for frontend and backend applications. Users can follow the provided Azure CLI commands and YAML manifest examples to implement this setup, ensuring that pods are scheduled on the appropriate nodes based on their specified tolerations and selectors. Additionally, a comparison table of scheduling features has been added, outlining the use cases and behaviors of taints, node selectors, node affinity, and inter-pod affinity, helping users choose the right approach for their needs.

The documentation now clarifies that Fleet Manager supports both Azure-hosted AKS clusters and Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes clusters as member clusters. Additionally, a new feature, SecurityPatch, has been introduced, which provides AKS-managed security patches applied to the existing VHD running on Linux node images. Users can also now connect to the same Git repository multiple times to deploy different resources or branches from that repository.
The Get-AksEdgeEventLog PowerShell command collects event logs from the deployment, which is crucial for troubleshooting and monitoring the health of AKS Edge deployments.
This document has been archived, indicating that the Get-AksHciCredential PowerShell command is no longer available for use.
Merged changes from the main branch, which may have included updates to the documentation for testing AKS Edge deployments, improving clarity and usability for users.

The New-AksHciProxySetting PowerShell command documentation has been updated to include detailed descriptions of parameters and examples for configuring proxy settings for AKS hybrid deployments. This includes information on how to set up proxy credentials and certificates.

The Update-AksHciClusterCertificates PowerShell command rotates tokens and certificates of all clients in the workload cluster. This command is essential for maintaining security and operational integrity within AKS hybrid environments.

This document provides a guide on how to configure Kueue with the AKS cluster autoscaler to effectively manage AI workloads. It includes detailed instructions and best practices for provisioning capacity for batch jobs using the autoscaler.
Removed the entire document related to the New-AksEdgeScaleConfig PowerShell command, which included details on creating configurations for scaling the cluster.
The Start-AksEdgeWorkerNodeUpdate PowerShell command is detailed in this document, which updates worker nodes as part of the update process for AKS Edge, ensuring that nodes are kept up to date.

The documentation now highlights fixes in the AKS on Azure Local for cluster upgrades and telemetry pod resource consumption. Users can expect improved functionality when creating, scaling, and upgrading AKS clusters due to resolved issues with VM image availability, as well as reduced CPU and memory usage from the telemetry pod. Additionally, deletion issues related to pod disruption budgets have been addressed, enhancing the overall cluster management experience.

This quickstart provides instructions on deploying an AKS cluster in AKS Hybrid and Edge on VMware using the Azure CLI. It includes prerequisites and important notes regarding the retirement of AKS on VMware on March 16, 2026, recommending users to transition to AKS on Azure Local for enhanced capabilities.

This document discusses the networking requirements for AKS Hybrid and Edge on VMware, including the importance of setting up networking correctly for Kubernetes clusters. It highlights the use of VMware logical network segments for IP address allocation, which is essential for cluster communication.
Updated the instructions for navigating to the resource group in the Azure portal, changing 'navigate to resource groups' to 'go to resource groups'.
The Uninstall-AksHciCsiNfs PowerShell command uninstalls the CSI NFS plugin in a cluster. It includes syntax and examples for usage.

The document provides troubleshooting guidance for issues encountered when deleting AKS clusters with PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) resources. It includes mitigation strategies and workarounds, which are vital for users managing AKS clusters.
The Install-AksHciCsiSmb PowerShell command installs the CSI SMB plugin to a cluster. It includes syntax and examples for usage.

The documentation now clarifies that Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) is supported for AKS on Azure Local for multi-rack deployments, allowing users to enable it by setting `enableAzureRBAC` to `true` during cluster creation. Additionally, users can access their Kubernetes cluster using either direct mode or proxy mode, with specific permissions required for each method, enhancing the flexibility and security of cluster management.

The documentation now correctly reflects that Ubuntu 20.04 is the default OS version for Kubernetes versions 1.24 to 1.34, while Ubuntu 24.04 is the default for Kubernetes versions 1.35 to 1.38. This change ensures users have accurate information regarding the supported OS versions for their AKS deployments.
The Set-AksHciRegistration command registers Azure Kubernetes Service on AKS hybrid with Azure, facilitating the connection and management of hybrid deployments.
The index for AKS Edge Essentials PowerShell commands provides a comprehensive list of cmdlets available for managing AKS Edge deployments, enhancing user accessibility to command documentation.

The Get-AksEdgeManagedServiceToken PowerShell command retrieves the managed service token for AKS Edge. This update is significant for users needing to authenticate and manage their AKS Edge deployments securely.

The Get-AksHciKubernetesVersion PowerShell command retrieves the current Kubernetes version for AKS hybrid clusters. This update ensures users can easily check their Kubernetes version, which is essential for compatibility and support.
The Enable-AksHciArcConnection command enables the Arc connection on an AKS hybrid cluster, allowing integration with Azure Arc for enhanced management and monitoring capabilities.
The Add-AksHciGmsaCredentialSpec PowerShell command documentation has been removed, which previously described how to add a credentials spec for gMSA deployments on a cluster.
The troubleshooting guide for AKS Hybrid and Edge on VMware provides steps for resolving common issues. This is essential for users to effectively manage and troubleshoot their deployments.

The Get-AksHciConfig PowerShell command lists the current configuration settings for the Azure Kubernetes Service host. This update ensures users can easily access and verify their configuration settings, which is vital for troubleshooting and management.

The Get-AksHciCluster command lists Kubernetes managed clusters, including the Azure Kubernetes Service host. This command provides users with the ability to view all clusters and specific details about them.
The New-AksHciNetworkSetting command creates a new virtual network for AKS hybrid deployments. This is crucial for configuring network settings that meet specific deployment requirements.

The documentation now includes detailed instructions for deleting an AKS cluster that has PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) resources, which may prevent successful deletion. Users are guided to first delete all PDBs using specific commands based on the cluster's connectivity state before attempting to delete the cluster or node pool. This change enhances clarity on the necessary steps to avoid deletion failures related to PDBs.
The Get-AksHciClusterNetwork PowerShell command retrieves information about cluster networks in AKS hybrid. It includes syntax, parameters, and examples for managing cluster networks.

The Set-AksHciConfig command documentation has been removed, indicating a significant change in how configuration settings for AKS hybrid hosts are managed. Users will need to adapt to new methods for configuration.
This document describes the Get-AksHciUpdates PowerShell command, which lists available updates for AKS on Azure Local and Windows Server, helping users keep their environments up to date.

The 'Uninstall-AksHciCsiSmb' command is described, detailing the process to uninstall the CSI SMB plug-in from a cluster. This is important for users managing their AKS hybrid environments, providing necessary syntax and examples.

The documentation for the Add-AksHciNode PowerShell command has been removed, indicating a significant change in the available commands for managing AKS hybrid environments. This could impact users relying on this command for adding nodes.
The Set-AksHciCluster PowerShell command scales the number of control plane nodes and enables or disables the autoscaler. It includes syntax, parameters, and examples for usage.

This document outlines the New-AksHciAutoScalerProfile command, which creates an autoscaler configuration profile for AKS hybrid. This feature allows for dynamic scaling of node pools based on workload demands.
This document provides instructions for using the Get-AksEdgeKubeConfig command to retrieve the KubeConfig file from an AKS Edge cluster. This is essential for managing and accessing the cluster.

This document outlines the troubleshooting and support policy for AKS Hybrid and Edge on VMware, including known issues and their workarounds. It emphasizes that AKS on VMware is in public preview and not recommended for production workloads, with a retirement date set for March 16, 2026.
The Get-AksHciClusterUpdates command retrieves available upgrades for an Azure Kubernetes Service cluster, helping users keep their clusters updated with the latest features and security patches.

The Repair-AksHciCerts PowerShell command documentation has been updated to indicate that this cmdlet will be deprecated and users should transition to using Update-AksHciCertificates. The documentation includes examples and parameter descriptions.

Merged changes from the main branch, which likely included updates to the documentation for removing a physical node from an AKS hybrid deployment, enhancing the clarity and usability of the command reference.

The documentation for the Get-AksHciStorageContainer PowerShell command has been updated to include new examples and clearer descriptions of its functionality, enhancing user understanding of how to manage storage containers in AKS.
The New-AksHciLoadBalancerSetting command creates a load balancer object for workload clusters in AKS hybrid. It includes syntax and important notes regarding deployment without a load balancer.

This document outlines the AKS Hybrid and Edge on VMware, emphasizing the retirement of AKS on VMware (preview) on March 16, 2026. It recommends deploying AKS on Azure Local for enhanced capabilities and details the integration of Azure Arc for managing Kubernetes clusters on VMware vSphere.
The New-AksEdgeConfig PowerShell command creates the configurations needed for a new AKS Edge Essentials deployment, facilitating the setup of new clusters.
Removed outdated troubleshooting documentation related to the AKS telemetry pod, streamlining the content and ensuring users have access to relevant and current information.

The Remove-AksHciAutoScalerProfile PowerShell command is introduced, which allows users to remove an unused autoscaler configuration profile from the system. This is important for maintaining a clean and efficient configuration environment.

The document has been updated to include a new 'SecurityPatch' channel for the Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager, which allows for the application of security patches to Linux nodes. This update enhances the orchestration of updates across multiple clusters.

The documentation for AKS on Azure has been updated to reflect the transition of the ms.custom parameter from "local" to "hyperconverged," indicating a shift in focus for users. Additionally, a note has been added regarding potential issues when deleting AKS clusters with PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) resources, informing users that the deletion may fail and that Microsoft is working on a fix. Users are advised to consult the troubleshooting guide for specific instructions on deleting workload identity-enabled AKS clusters.
The document discusses known issues with Kubernetes cluster creation or node pool scaling due to AKS image problems. This information is vital for troubleshooting and ensuring successful deployments.

The Uninstall-AksHciMonitoring PowerShell command provides a method to remove monitoring components from AKS hybrid clusters. This update includes necessary details for users to effectively clean up their monitoring setup.
Removed the entire document related to the Repair-AksEdgeKms PowerShell command, which included details on repairing the KMS plugin.
The Stop-AksEdgeNode PowerShell command stops the node VM if it is currently started. It provides syntax, parameters, and examples for usage, including options for specifying node types.

This document outlines the scale requirements for AKS Hybrid and Edge on VMware, detailing the supported scale counts for clusters and node pools. This information is critical for users planning their deployments to ensure they meet the necessary infrastructure requirements.

The Get-AksHciAutoScalerProfile PowerShell command retrieves a list of autoscaler configuration profiles or a specific profile's settings, providing users with essential information for managing scaling in AKS hybrid environments.

This document provides an overview of the AKS on VMware workload cluster architecture, detailing the components and infrastructure necessary for deploying and managing Kubernetes clusters effectively.
The Set-AksEdgeNodeToDrain PowerShell command prepares to remove a node from an existing cluster by safely draining it, which is important for maintenance and upgrades.

The Set-AksHciNodePool PowerShell command allows users to scale a node pool within a Kubernetes cluster. It includes syntax, parameters, and examples for configuring the number of nodes and enabling or disabling the horizontal node autoscaler.

The documentation now includes a new section that provides a complete example for creating a dynamically provisioned Azure Files volume, including a StorageClass, PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC), and a pod that mounts the file share. Users can follow the detailed steps to create a file named `azure-file-dynamic.yaml`, apply it using `kubectl`, and verify the PVC and pod states, enhancing their ability to manage Azure Files in AKS. Additionally, the example specifies using the `Standard_LRS` SKU and SMB protocol, which helps users understand the configuration for production workloads.

This document provides details on the Uninstall-AksHci PowerShell command, which removes AKS hybrid. It includes important notes on configuration cleanup and the implications of running commands on clusters previously deployed with Windows Admin Center.
The New-AksHciStorageContainer PowerShell command creates a new storage container, which is essential for managing storage in AKS hybrid environments.

The Get-AksHciNodePool PowerShell command lists the node pools in a Kubernetes cluster, providing syntax and examples for usage. It includes parameters for specifying the cluster name and node pool name, enhancing user guidance for managing AKS hybrid environments.
This document outlines the system requirements and support matrix for AKS Hybrid and Edge on VMware. Understanding these requirements is crucial for successful deployment and operation.

This document describes the Invoke-AksHciRotateCACertificate PowerShell command, which is used to rotate the cloud agent CA certificates for AKS hybrid. This is crucial for maintaining security in hybrid deployments.

The documentation now clarifies that starting with AKS version 1.31, container images are pulled in parallel by default, improving performance compared to the previous serialized method. Users are encouraged to upgrade to a currently supported AKS version to take advantage of this feature. Additionally, new guidance has been added on using ephemeral OS disks, increasing managed OS disk sizes, and utilizing newer VM sizes to enhance performance during image pulls.
This guide explains how to install and uninstall the Kubernetes Extension for AKS Operators, detailing the steps necessary for onboarding Arc-enabled VMware vSphere to Azure.
The Get-AksEdgeNodeConnectivityMode PowerShell command retrieves the connectivity mode of the AKS Edge Essentials Linux node, which is important for understanding network configurations.
Merged changes from the main branch, which may have included updates to the documentation for installing the gMSA webhook addon, improving clarity and usability for users.
Updated the service tag from 'azure-appgw-for-containers' to 'azure-application-gateway-containers'. This change aligns the documentation with the current naming conventions for Azure services.
Removed the entire document related to the Install-AksEdgeHostFeatures PowerShell command, which included details on installing missing required OS features.

The Test-UpdateAksHci command checks whether any target clusters are outside the support window for the latest version of AKS hybrid. This is crucial for maintaining compliance and ensuring clusters are up to date.

The documentation now clarifies that the NVIDIA driver is preinstalled in the worker VM image, eliminating the need for manual installation. Users are instructed to verify the preinstalled driver using `nvidia-smi` and to install the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and NVIDIA Kubernetes device plugin to ensure GPU schedulability. Additionally, the steps for verifying the driver and GPU presence have been updated to reflect this change, enhancing the overall setup process for GPU node pools in AKS Arc.

Specifically, the AKS range for Istio 1.3 has been corrected to include versions 1.30 to 1.35, and the range for Istio 1.4 has been expanded to include version 1.36. Additionally, the expected release date for Istio 1.2 has been updated to May 2026.

The documentation now clarifies that access controls for Kubernetes Custom Resources (CRs) are currently not supported for roles using Managed Fleet Namespaces for multi-cluster multi-tenancy. Additionally, the preview designation has been removed from the section title, indicating that users can expect a more stable feature set.

The documentation now specifies that the Ubuntu with containerd and FIPS node image is not supported for Ubuntu 24.04+, rather than 22.04+, and clarifies that it cannot be combined with Arm64 or CVM. Additionally, the Ubuntu with containerd and Trusted Launch node image documentation has been updated to reflect that it cannot be combined with Arm64 or CVM, removing the mention of FIPS. These changes provide clearer guidance on compatibility for users configuring their node images.

The documentation now includes guidance on adding a node pool with both Trusted Launch and FIPS enabled, specifically for Ubuntu 22.04 node pools on Generation 2 VM sizes. Users can utilize the `az aks nodepool add` command to create this configuration, which includes parameters for enabling secure boot and vTPM. Additionally, the documentation clarifies that Trusted Launch cannot be enabled in the same node pool as Arm64, Pod Sandboxing, or Confidential VM, and provides examples for checking the node pool's Trusted Launch status.

The documentation for Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager has been updated to clarify that it enables at-scale management of hundreds of Kubernetes clusters. Users can now utilize "Managed Fleet Namespaces" to grant application teams access to namespaces across multiple clusters, and they can include optional manual or automated approvals for update groups and stages to enhance control over update applications. Additionally, the overview page now reflects updated statistics regarding the number of Kubernetes clusters and update runs.
Updated instructions for upgrading Windows OS in AKS, including clarifications on the nodeSelector field in deployment YAML.

The documentation now clarifies that for associations created on or after April 23, 2026, Network Security Groups (NSGs) are fully supported on the Application Gateway for Containers association subnet, including both inbound and outbound rules. Additionally, it specifies that "Deny all" rules can block traffic on ports 80 and 443 unless explicit allow rules are added, which may prevent access to the frontend and impact communication with the AKS cluster. Users are advised to ensure that necessary exceptions are configured to maintain proper functionality.
Learn how to enable and use Azure role-based access control (RBAC) with Microsoft Entra ID to authorize Kubernetes API requests on AKS on Azure Local for multi-rack deployments.

The documentation now specifies that when upgrading a supported AKS cluster, users must perform upgrades sequentially by minor version number, rather than major version number, which was previously stated. Additionally, the supported Kubernetes versions for ALRS/HAKS multi-rack have been updated to include versions up to 1.34.7, and example outputs have been revised to reflect the latest version 1.33.11. Users can now see the correct command to upgrade to version 1.34.7 using the Azure CLI.

The documentation now includes a breaking changes table for Kubernetes version 1.36, detailing updates to AKS managed add-ons and components, which users should review to understand potential impacts on their deployments. Additionally, the end-of-life date for Kubernetes version 1.33 has been updated to July 2026, and a release calendar entry for Kubernetes version 1.37 has been added, indicating its preview in September 2026 and general availability in October 2026.

The documentation now clarifies that the `controlPlaneIp` parameter is optional during cluster creation and will default to the host machine's IP address if omitted. Users are advised to specify a custom IP only if they require the control plane to be reachable on a different address, and if using DHCP, they must reserve the control plane IP to ensure it remains permanently assigned to the machine to avoid cluster inaccessibility.

The documentation now includes detailed settings for configuring Linux custom OS parameters in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), specifically under the `LinuxOSConfig` section. Users can adjust file handle limits, socket and network tuning settings, worker limit settings, and virtual memory settings, with specific YAML examples provided for each configuration. Additionally, users are advised to carefully test any changes in nonproduction environments before applying them.

The documentation now includes a new section detailing the failure of geo-replica creation when a registry's private endpoint is configured with static IP allocation. Users are informed that adding a geo-replica fails because the static configuration does not automatically provision the necessary data endpoint members, and they are provided with specific commands to check the private IP allocation method. Additionally, recommended solutions are outlined, advising users to either use dynamic IP allocation for future geo-replicas or to create the private endpoint after all geo-replicas have been established if static allocation is necessary.

The documentation now includes important notes regarding the configuration of the Istio add-on with Azure Load Balancer annotations for the `Gateway` Service. Users must unset specific health probe annotations in the `GatewayClass` or per-`Gateway` ConfigMap when setting `spec.externalTrafficPolicy` to "Local." This clarification helps ensure proper health probe configuration and functionality.

The documentation now specifies that dedicated data endpoints are a prerequisite for enabling IPv6 dual-stack endpoints, allowing users to set their endpoint protocol to `IPv4AndIPv6`. Additionally, the validity period for temporary download links during image pulls has been updated to indicate that they are valid for at least 20 minutes and up to 30 minutes, enhancing security for downloading image layers.
Learn how to deploy an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster on bare metal using an ARM template.

The documentation now includes detailed information about API request rate limits for Azure Container Registry (ACR), specifying limits based on the SKU (Basic, Standard, Premium) and operation categories such as DataplaneRead, DataplaneWrite, and DataplaneDelete. Users can expect to receive an HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` error if their request rate exceeds these limits, along with a `Retry-After` header indicating how long to wait before retrying. This enhancement allows users to better manage their API usage and understand the implications of exceeding request limits.

The documentation now clarifies that the control plane IP is an optional field during cluster creation, defaulting to the host machine's IP if left blank. Users are advised to reserve the control plane IP address if using DHCP to ensure it remains permanently assigned, as changes to this IP can render the Kubernetes cluster unreachable. Additionally, the requirements for naming the cluster have been updated to specify that names must be 1-27 characters long and can only include letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores.

The documentation now includes detailed information about Envoy access logging, which is enabled by default on all managed `Gateway` proxy pods. Users can view access logs using the `kubectl logs` command, which provides insights into HTTP methods, paths, response codes, and sizes, facilitating easier troubleshooting of ingress traffic. Additionally, the guide has been updated to clarify the integration of Azure DNS and TLS for hostname management with the application routing Gateway API implementation.
